summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 1 diabetes, poorly controlled due to medication noncompliance, alcohol use disorder, and depression, presented with altered mental status and was found to be in severe diabetic ketoacidosis with a glucose of 1214, pH of 6.92, and anion gap of 56. She had hyperkalemia, acute kidney injury with creatinine rising to 2.8, and hypotension requiring pressor support. Due to worsening acidosis and respiratory fatigue, she was intubated and admitted to the MICU. She received an insulin drip, IV fluids, bicarbonate, and temporary hemodialysis via a right internal jugular line. Her course improved with correction of metabolic abnormalities, and she was transitioned to subcutaneous insulin. She had a non-ST elevation myocardial infarction likely due to demand ischemia, managed medically with metoprolol, aspirin, and atorvastatin. Psychiatry initiated Zoloft and arranged for a dual-diagnosis partial hospitalization program. Her renal function recovered, and she was discharged home with services, improved mental status, and a plan for ongoing behavioral and medical follow-up.
